newsitem.title: FRANCE: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MARSEILLE LOOK TOWARDS BRIGHT FUTURE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER SHOWCASE-MARSEILLE LOOK TOWARDS BRIGHT FUTURE.

text.p: Marseille's new chairman Robert Louis-Dreyfus believes there is a team with European potential in the making at the Velodrome once more.

"This team is starting to have a game structure and has learnt to handle better the difficult moments (of a match)," Louis-Dreyfus said after Marseille's 3-0 home win over French champions Auxerre on Sunday.

"This is important given that Europe remains our target," added Louis-Dreyfus, who officially took charge of the club on Friday after it had a spell in the hands of city authorities following the fall of Bernard Tapie.
The victory, the second in six days over Auxerre after Marseille put them out of the League Cup on Tuesday, extended the 1993 European Cup winners' unbeaten run in the first division to seven games.
Now Louis-Dreyfus would like to see Marseille win away for the first time this season when they travel to Rennes on Friday for their last game before the winter break.

It will be no easy task. Rennes, 12th two places behind Marseille, may have an abysmal away record with only two points out of a possible 36, but they have the best at home tally in the first division with eight wins and two draws.
Jean-Michel Roussier, Marseille's executive president, said: "Like all the big teams, we've always done well against Auxerre. Now we must manage to overcome the lesser teams that come here."

Marseille, whose unbeaten run started with a 3-1 home win over current leaders Monaco and included a 0-0 draw away to then pacesetters Paris Saint-Germain, dropped an alarming number of points against lowly teams earlier in the season.
Their slump in October, during which the fans turned against big name players such as Bulgaria's Yordan Lechkov, included successive 1-0 home defeats to Caen and Nantes.
Lechkov lost favour with coach Gerard Gili but made a fine comeback in the 3-2 League Cup win before confirming his importance to the Marseille side in Sunday's victory.
"This is a squad on the way to becoming a team," said Gili. "They knew how to make their chances, take them and defend their gains. It's my great satisfaction."

His opposite number Guy Roux, unable to repeat at the Velodrome his upstaging of Ajax's Louis van Gaal in the new Amsterdam Arena in the European Cup, said: "Two defeats and a lot of regrets, a week to forget quickly."
Auxerre, fifth but only five points ahead of Marseille, had conceded only five goals away in domestic competition before their double visit to the Velodrome where they let in six.

Marseille's defence is backed by Germany's sound goalkeeper Andreas Koepke, while the centre-back pairing of Italians Ivan Franceschini and Alberto Malusci improves with each game as does Englishman Chris Makin on the flank.

In midfield, they have strengthened the promotion side with Lechkov, France's Reynald Pedros and Eric Roy, while up front the need for a regular scorer of goals looks less pressing after the half dozen they put past Auxerre.
After the news that Marseille were after Valencia's Croatian Goran Vlaovic, former French international Xavier Gravelaine hit his sixth goal of the season on Sunday.
But what has probably given most pleasure to Gili is the form of Marseille's own products.
Striker Marc Libbra and defender Hamada Jambay both scored a goal apiece in the two wins over Auxerre.

Midfielder Ludovic Asuar laid on the goal for Jambay on Sunday as a substitute. He displaced Lechkov in October but now looks more likely to play with rather than instead of the Bulgarian World Cup semifinalist.
